Download VerseKit: ready in three steps

Free, no account, for Windows and Linux. After that the program tells you about new versions itself.

  1. Download

    An installer on Windows, a single file on Linux.

    Windows

    Installer

    VerseKit-Setup.exe Download for Windows

    Linux

    Single file

    VerseKit-x86_64.AppImage Download for Linux

    The buttons always download the latest version. See all versions

  2. Launch and set up

    On first start a wizard walks you through setup: language, finding Star Citizen, collecting your existing blueprints. It takes a minute.

    On first start Windows says “Windows protected your PC”. That happens with every program without an expensive certificate. Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. The readme explains it with pictures.

    On Linux, make the file executable once: right-click, Properties, “Allow executing file as program”.

  3. Play

    Start Star Citizen as usual. VerseKit reads along and reports new blueprints at once. The program tells you about new versions itself and installs them at the push of a button.

Check it is genuine

Every version comes with a checksum. The value your system prints must appear in SHA256SUMS.txt Otherwise do not run the file.

Windows (Command Prompt in your downloads folder)

certutil -hashfile VerseKit-Setup.exe SHA256

Linux

sha256sum VerseKit-x86_64.AppImage

Virus scan: VirusTotal report for the current version

Is it safe?

The fair question before any download. Here is what VerseKit does and what it does not.

  • No hooks into the game

    No access to the game's memory, nothing is injected. VerseKit reads the logs Star Citizen writes itself, and only changes files you could also edit by hand. The only exception is the anti-AFK (Windows only, off by default): when switched on, it presses Alt+X every 5 minutes, just as you would yourself.

  • Open source

    Every line is public on GitHub. The files you download are built by GitHub itself from exactly this code.

  • Verified updates

    Every version comes with a checksum. An update is only installed if the file matches it exactly.

  • Free, no catch

    No paid tier, no ads, no sign-up. An error report only goes out when you send it yourself.

  • Stays with you

    No account, no cloud, no personal data. VerseKit only fetches reference data from sources that are meant for it, and counts itself once a day: without any ID, and you can switch that off.

The build has every version checked on VirusTotal; “Check it is genuine” above links the report. Individual scanners occasionally flag packed Python programs through machine-learning heuristics. That is a known false positive.

VerseKit is an unofficial fan project and is not affiliated with Cloud Imperium Games.
